CallShape.description:
The calls of a flagged symbol that the flag is about; any other call is the API as it was.

A call is one if it passes a keyword of `keywords`, has more positional arguments than
`positional_from`, leaves out a name of `omits` (given by keyword, or by position at its index;
null for a name only a keyword can give), or has a `*` argument, which can pass the positions,
or a `**` argument, which can pass the keywords and the names. `bases` says the class's bases
changed, which no call passes: only code that derives from it, or uses it other than as a call,
an import, an annotation or an argument, is affected.
CallShape.title: CallShape

ChatHistory.description: A chat history, whose bare-string parts are wrapped under `text_key` for the new SDK.
ChatHistory.title: ChatHistory

ExternalFixerParams.description:
A maintained tool's rewrite of a legacy surface, held to the proof of a rule's own.

`symbols` are the legacy names the tool rewrites where they are used: the scan finds them as it
does for any change, and only the lines it reports may change (ADR-074).
ExternalFixerParams.title: ExternalFixerParams

FlagOnlyParams.description: Symbols, string patterns and removed attributes a pack refuses, and what it says instead.
FlagOnlyParams.title: FlagOnlyParams

Layout.description: The maximum line width the pack's rules emit; match it to the user's formatter.
Layout.title: Layout

Legacy.description:
The old side, which may also say which release an unversioned declaration stands for.

`newest` is what an unversioned declaration installs, so it stands for a version nothing in the
repository wrote down. It is the pack's claim, checked weekly against the index. `lacks` names
what that release no longer defines, which the code may still use. `since` is the other way,
for a distribution whose newest release is on the new side: the names no release below the
floor of `version` defines, so code that uses one was written for a release `version` admits.
Legacy.title: Legacy

ManifestDependencyParams.description:
The pin edit; both names may be one distribution, whose major version is the migration.

`declare_transitive` lets the pin move while a file imports a module only the legacy
distribution installed (`match.transitive`) and no manifest of its app declares it: each such
distribution is declared, unpinned, on a line below the legacy requirement.
ManifestDependencyParams.title: ManifestDependencyParams

Match.description: What the scanner looks for before any rule runs.
Match.title: Match

MethodRewrite.description: How one legacy method of a declared receiver becomes a call in the new SDK.
MethodRewrite.title: MethodRewrite

PackSource.description: Where and when the migration facts were read; the optional `sha256` hashes that page.
PackSource.title: PackSource

PluginChange.description:
A change made by a plugin's rule; its `params` are read by the plugin's own model, when the
plugin is loaded, since nothing here can say what they hold.
PluginChange.title: PluginChange

PluginRequirement.description:
A rule kind the user's own plugin provides, and the releases of its distribution a pack was
written against. The pack names the plugin by its entry point and trusts nothing about it:
whether it may run is the user's to say (`plugins` in `~/.config/obelize/config.yml`).
PluginRequirement.title: PluginRequirement

RenameMemberParams.description:
Members of a class that the new release spells another way, wherever an instance is seen.

An instance of the class, or of one that derives from it, is renamed the same: a pack names
the class that defines the members, and what derives from it in the repository is found.
RenameMemberParams.title: RenameMemberParams

RenameSettingParams.description: Module settings the new release spells another way, assigned as the old ones were.
RenameSettingParams.title: RenameSettingParams

RenameSymbolParams.description:
Names a kept package or module defined, which the new release spells another way.

`symbols` are the names a submodule defined that the new release exports from the package
above it. `renamed` are the names that stay where they are and take another spelling.
RenameSymbolParams.title: RenameSymbolParams

RewriteCallParams.description: One legacy free function and the client call it becomes; unlisted parameters are refused.
RewriteCallParams.title: RewriteCallParams

RewritePatternParams.description:
A call of a name, written as the new release spells it, found by a pattern of its shape.

`before` is a call, `after` the expression that replaces it, and `$name` stands for any
expression `before` has in that place. The call is of a qualified name written out
(`pydantic.parse_obj_as($type, $value)`) or of a member of a class (`$m.dict(exclude=$e)`, with
`where` naming the class `$m` is an instance of). `after` may also spell names through the
modules `imports` lists, imported if the file has no name for them (ADR-071 D4).
RewritePatternParams.title: RewritePatternParams

SafetySettings.description: The safety table: legacy safety strings and enum members, and the new members they become.
SafetySettings.title: SafetySettings

Target.description:
The new side, which also says which Pythons it installs on.

A distribution says it as `requires_python`; a side that is the Pythons themselves says it as
`python`. Either way it is the set a repository's declared Python must stay inside (ADR-050 D4).
`introduces` names what no release of `from.version` defines, where one module holds both
sides: code that uses one cannot run on a pin that admits only the old releases.
Target.title: Target

Verification.description: Commands a pack suggests as display text; obelize never runs them, under any flag.
Verification.title: Verification

description:
One migration between two versions of one SDK, as declarative data.

This schema states the shape of each value. PEP 440 specifiers, sorted order and every rule that
compares two fields are checked by `obelize pack validate`, which is authoritative.
title: PackDocument
